review_type: source-grounded AI review; not physician adjudication
reviewed_components: all clinical facts and measured quantities
corrections: Reworded the cardiac-surgery limitation to the source wording ('at least 7 (7%) acquired RSV infection following cardiac surgery', not 'deaths followed cardiac surgery') and recorded that it is a lower bound consistent with the Discussion's limited-data statement, not a conflict (7/96 is a rounding difference).
Sharpened the n = 17 (Methods, population unstated) versus n = 19 nosocomial (sensitivity analysis) limitation as an unreconciled ambiguity.

Rewrote the supplement limitation: SD1 is a Word document (Supplemental Digital Content 1 to 10, including a native Word chart with an embedded workbook) plus a PDF (Supplemental Digital Content 11, collaborators).
Added a limitation for article-versus-supplement aggregate discrepancies (LMIC median hospital stay 7 vs 6.5 vs 6.0 days; embedded workbook cross-tabulations totalling 224 deaths vs 231).
Corrected the b00043 source-coverage note: it is the Table 1 footnote, not a table row.
unresolved: Disposition aggregate_only: the source is a global registry case series that reports 231 nosocomial RSV-related in-hospital deaths only as counts, percentages and medians; no death has individual identity evidence or a case narrative, so no individual patient records are created and group statistics are not copied to placeholder patients.
reported_individual_count is 231 (the literal number of deaths included) and roster_complete is false because none of the 231 individuals can be enumerated.

Table 1 reports the nosocomial and the community-acquired groups side by side; the community-acquired group (n = 931) comes from the registry, partly previously published deaths, and is not recorded as patient data of this article.

The Results state that 80 deaths were identified through the literature search and 188 comprised unpublished reports, which sum to more than the 231 deaths included; the text does not itself state how the two figures relate to 231. The Figure 1 flowchart carries the exclusion step, but values printed inside images are pixel content only and are not used as facts. This is an arithmetic ambiguity and is not reconciled.

The Methods state that comorbidity or prematurity data were not reported for n = 17 children (assumed otherwise healthy and born at term) without saying whether this count covers nosocomial deaths only, while the sensitivity analysis states n = 19 nosocomial deaths (and n = 231 community-acquired deaths) with missing comorbidity or prematurity data. The relation between 17 and 19 is not stated; this is an unreconciled ambiguity, not a fact.

The Results state that of the 96 children with congenital heart disease 'at least 7 (7%) acquired RSV infection following cardiac surgery', while the Discussion states that the authors have limited data on whether these children acquired RSV infection during admission for cardiac surgery because this was not part of the questionnaire. The two statements are consistent with a lower bound and are not a source conflict; 7 of 96 is about 7.3%, a rounding difference. Recorded only as aggregate context; no individual is identified.

The supplement SD1 consists of a Word document (Supplemental Digital Content 1 to 10: search string, contributing publications, country-of-origin counts, group-level characteristic tables, a forest-plot image and a native Word age-band chart with an embedded workbook) and a PDF (Supplemental Digital Content 11: collaborator names and affiliations). Its contents are reviewed in the supplement document sidecar and manifest, not here; everything in it is registry-level, literature-level or administrative, and no individual patient is described.

Figures 1-3 are registry-level graphics (flowchart, location map, age-distribution chart) and are not attributable to any individual patient; the chart in Figure 3 plots proportions by age band for three income groups, and no values are read from bar heights.

Aggregate figures differ between the article and the supplement without explanation: the article gives a median hospital stay of 7 days for nosocomial deaths from LMICs, while Supplemental Digital Content 4 prints 6.5 (3.0-17.5) and Supplemental Digital Content 6 prints 6.0 (3.0-17.5) days; the workbook embedded behind the Supplemental Digital Content 10 chart holds age-band cross-tabulations totalling 224 deaths (LIC/LMIC 28, UMIC 76, HIC 120) instead of the 231 (32, 76, 123) reported in the article. These are group-level discrepancies that affect no patient record; they are recorded, not reconciled.

key_findings: Read all 57 segments, including the 27 Table 1 rows, the footnote and 3 captions. This is a registry case series of 231 nosocomial RSV in-hospital deaths reported only as counts, percentages, medians and odds ratios. No death is individuated anywhere, so aggregate_only with patients [] is correct. The roster is 231 (b00014 literal) with roster_complete false.

Read all 284 units of the supplement docx and the embedded forest-plot image. I also opened the native Word chart (word/charts/chart1.xml) and its embedded workbook (3 sheets of SPSS cross-tabulations and chart data), which the extractor does not inventory. All of it is aggregate, with no per-patient row or case narrative. The 8 PDF pages are collaborator names and affiliations only.

80 + 188 = 268 vs 231: the text does not reconcile these numbers. The Figure 1 pixels print an exclusion of 37 deaths after data-quality assessment (268 - 37 = 231), but that is pixel content only, so the limitation stays an arithmetic ambiguity.

Figure 2 has 38 printed circle integers, with no legend and no country labels. The integers sum to 231, which I checked only as a pixel cross-check and did not use as a fact. Figure 3 and the supplement forest plot carry no data labels; their qualitative descriptions contain no positional readings.
residual_risks: The supplement's per-country table (Supplemental Digital Content 3) could be used to attribute the Figure 2 circles to countries. This was deliberately not done in the article annotation or the visual record.
The embedded workbook behind the Supplemental Digital Content 10 chart is outside the text-document extraction contract. Its aggregate numbers (total 224) are recorded only as a limitation.
